source_text:
Καὶ μὴ λεγέτω ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ λόγῳ τῷ κατὰ Ἀστέριον Οὐρβανὸν τὸ διὰ Μαξιμίλλης πνεῦμα, διώκομαι ὡς λύκος ἐκ προβάτων· οὐκ εἰμὶ λύκος· ῥῆμα εἰμὶ καὶ πνεῦμα καὶ δύναμις. ἀλλὰ τὴν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι δύναμιν ἐναργῶς δειξάτω καὶ ἐλεγξάτω· καὶ ἐξομολογεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καταναγκασάτω τοὺς τότε παρόντας· εἰς τὸ δοκιμάσαι καὶ διαλεχθῆναι τῷ πνεύματι λαλοῦντι, ἄνδρας δοκίμους καὶ ἐπισκόπους, Ζωτικὸν ἀπὸ Κομάνης κώμης, καὶ Ἰουλιανὸν ἀπὸ Ἀπαμείας. ὧν οἱ περὶ Θεμίσωνα τὰ στόματα φιμώσαντες, οὐκ εἴασαν τὸ ψευδὲς καὶ λαοπλάνον πνεῦμα ὑπ’ αὐτῶν ἐλεγχθῆναι. ἐν ταυτῷ δὲ πάλιν ἕτερα μεταξὺ πρὸς ἔλεγχον τῶν τῆς Μαξιμίλλης ψυδοπροφητειῶν εἰπὼν, ὁμοῦ τόν τε χρόνον καθ’ ὃν ταῦτ’ ἔγραφε σημαίνει, καὶ τῶν προῤῥήσεων αὐτῆς μέμνηται, δι’ ὧν πολέμους ἔσεσθαι καὶ ἀκαταστασίας προεμαντεύσατο· ὧν καὶ τὴν ψευδολογίαν εὐθύνει ὧδε λέγων.
Καὶ πῶς οὐ καταφανὲς ἤδη γέγονε καὶ τοῦτο τὸ ψεῦδος; πλείω γὰρ ἢ τρισκαίδεκα ἔτη εἰς ταύτην τὴν ἡμέραν, ἐξ οὗ τετελεύτηκεν ἡ γυνή· καὶ οὔτε μερικὸς, οὔτε καθολικὸς κόσμῳ γέγονε πόλεμος· ἀλλὰ καὶ Χριστιανοῖς μᾶλλον εἰρήνη διάμονος ἐξ ἐλέους Θεοῦ.
thought_title: Testing the spirit that spoke through Maximilla
orientation: The author is refuting the Montanist claim by quoting Maximilla's own saying and then showing that the spirit speaking through her refused to be tested by bishops.
pass_a_gloss: And let not the spirit through Maximilla say in that same work against Asterius Urbanus: 'I am persecuted like a wolf from sheep; I am not a wolf; I am word and spirit and power.' But let it show clearly the power in the spirit and refute it; and let it compel those then present to confess through the spirit; for the testing and conversing with the spirit that was speaking, approved men and bishops, Zoticus from the village of Comana, and Julian from Apamea. The followers of Themison, having silenced their mouths, did not permit the false and people-deceiving spirit to be refuted by them. And in the same work again, having said other things in between for the refutation of the false prophecies of Maximilla, he indicates at once both the time at which he was writing these things, and he mentions her predictions, through which she foretold that there would be wars and disturbances; of which he also corrects the falsehood, saying as follows. And how has not this falsehood also already become manifest? For more than thirteen years have passed to this day, since the woman died; and neither a partial nor a universal war has happened in the world; but rather for Christians there is lasting peace from the mercy of God.

choices.why: Keeps the compound's force as a single pejorative modifier of spirit, matching the author's polemical tone.
Renders the demand for visible, manifest demonstration of power, not a hidden claim.
Preserves the strong force of compulsion the author demands from the spirit.
Keeps the vivid physical image of muzzling, which the author uses to describe the Montanists' suppression of the bishops.
Renders the adjective's sense of continuous, enduring peace, contrasting with the predicted wars.

pass_b_english: And let not the spirit speaking through Maximilla say, in that same work against Asterius Urbanus, “I am persecuted like a wolf from the sheep; I am not a wolf. I am word and spirit and power.” But let it clearly show the power in the spirit and let it be refuted. And let it compel those who were present then to confess through the spirit, so that men of repute and bishops, Zoticus from the village of Comana and Julian from Apamea, might test and speak with the spirit speaking. But the followers of Themison silenced their mouths and did not allow the false and people-deceiving spirit to be refuted by them.

Then again, after saying other things in between to refute the false prophecies of Maximilla, he at the same time indicates the time when he wrote these things and recalls her predictions, through which she foretold that there would be wars and upheavals. And he corrects their falsehood, speaking as follows:

And how has this lie not already become obvious? For it is more than thirteen years to this day since the woman died, and no war, either partial or universal, has come upon the world. On the contrary, there has been lasting peace for Christians, by the mercy of God.

problems.quote: so that the spirit speaking might be tested and questioned
problems.source_quote: εἰς τὸ δοκιμάσαι καὶ διαλεχθῆναι τῷ πνεύματι λαλοῦντι
problems.why: The bishops are to test and speak with the spirit, not the spirit be tested; infinitives have bishops as implied subject.
problems.fix: so that they might test and speak with the spirit
problems.ruling: Infinitives δοκιμάσαι, διαλεχθῆναι have implied subject of the men, not τῷ πνεύματι λαλοῦντι.

edits.old: so that the spirit speaking might be tested and questioned
edits.new: so that they might test and speak with the spirit speaking

fixed: Changed 'so that the spirit speaking might be tested and questioned' to 'so that they might test and speak with the spirit speaking' because the Greek infinitives δοκιμάσαι and διαλεχθῆναι have the bishops as implied subject, not the spirit.

problems.why: Priscilla named in intro only; in 2.1 'the women' then 'the woman mentioned above' unclear which woman, then Maximilla named.
problems.fix: Clarify Priscilla disappears from narrative; 'the woman' is Maximilla.

problems.quote: I am persecuted like a wolf from the sheep; I am not a wolf. I am word and spirit and power.
problems.why: Maximilla's words quoted, but 'let not the spirit speaking through Maximilla say' makes attribution complex; reader may miss this is direct quotation of Maximilla.
problems.fix: Clarify: direct quotation of Maximilla's oracular utterance.

problems.quote: And how has this lie not already become obvious? For it is more than thirteen years to this day since the woman died, and no war, either partial or universal, has come upon the world.
problems.why: Sudden shift to authorial voice after Eusebian framing; 'he corrects their falsehood, speaking as follows' introduces quote but reader may lose track of who speaks.

problems.quote: But let it clearly show the power in the spirit and refute it.
problems.why: Grammar breaks: 'let it [the spirit] show the power in the spirit and refute it'—refute what? The spirit refuting itself?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'let it prove its power and submit to testing.'

problems.quote: so that they might test and speak with the spirit speaking—men of repute and bishops, Zoticus from the village of Comana and Julian from Apamea.
problems.why: Dash insertion breaks syntax; 'test and speak with the spirit speaking' is garbled.
problems.fix: Reconstruct: 'so that these men of repute, the bishops Zoticus... and Julian..., might test and speak with the spirit.'

problems.quote: He even roused two other women
problems.why: Maximilla and Priscilla introduced vaguely, then referenced as 'the women' without naming them again.
problems.fix: Name Maximilla and Priscilla at first mention and clarify later references.

problems.quote: the followers of Themison silenced their mouths
problems.why: Montanist adherents called by different labels; Themison never explained.
problems.fix: Identify Themison as a Montanist leader at first mention.

problems.quote: Then again, after saying other things in between to refute the false prophecies of Maximilla, he at the same time indicates the time when he wrote these things
problems.why: 'He' shifts to a different author (Asterius Urbanus or Miltiades) without clear signal.
problems.fix: Specify who 'he' is—the author being quoted.

problems.quote: But let it clearly show the power in the spirit and refute it.
problems.why: Ambiguous pronouns: unclear what 'it' shows or what is refuted.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'let the spirit show power and let others refute it.'

edits.old: But let it clearly show the power in the spirit and refute it.
edits.new: But let it clearly show the power in the spirit and let it be refuted.

edits.old: so that they might test and speak with the spirit speaking—men of repute and bishops, Zoticus from the village of Comana and Julian from Apamea.
edits.new: so that men of repute and bishops, Zoticus from the village of Comana and Julian from Apamea, might test and speak with the spirit speaking.

fixed: The 'woman mentioned above' problem refers to a different section not in this text; no edit needed here.
The quotation is clearly introduced as the spirit speaking through Maximilla; no edit needed.
The authorial voice is clear from 'he corrects their falsehood, speaking as follows'; no edit needed.
Fixed: 'let it clearly show the power in the spirit and let it be refuted' clarifies that the spirit should be refuted by others.
Fixed: restructured the sentence so the bishops are the ones testing and speaking with the spirit.
The 'He even roused two other women' problem refers to a different section not in this text; no edit needed here.
Themison is identified as a Montanist leader in the cast list; no edit needed in this section.
The 'he' refers to the author of the work against Asterius Urbanus, as stated in the voice notes; no edit needed.
Fixed: same as the earlier 'let it clearly show' problem.

last_rejected.why: Object is missing: must refute the speakers/bishops, not 'it'.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐλεγξάτω takes τὴν … δύναμιν as its object, so ‘refute it’ (the power) is correct.

last_rejected.quote: compel those who were present then to confess through the spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐξομολογεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος καταναγκασάτω τοὺς τότε παρόντας
last_rejected.why: The spirit should compel confession, not compel them 'through the spirit'.
last_rejected.fix: let it compel through the spirit those present then to confess
last_rejected.ruling: καταναγκασάτω … διὰ τοῦ πνεύματος means compel … through/by the spirit, matching translation.

last_rejected.quote: so that they might test and speak with the spirit speaking
last_rejected.source_quote: εἰς τὸ δοκιμάσαι καὶ διαλεχθῆναι τῷ πνεύματι λαλοῦντι
last_rejected.why: Purpose clause misattributed: the testing/speaking is what the bishops came to do, not result of confession.
last_rejected.fix: men of repute and bishops who came to test and speak with the spirit
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς τὸ δοκιμάσαι … τῷ πνεύματι λαλοῦντι is a purpose clause for the listed men to test and speak with the spirit.

last_rejected.why: τὰ στόματα is object, not 'their mouths'; Themison's followers gagged the bishops.
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ στόματα is the object of φιμώσαντες; “silenced their mouths” conveys the same meaning.

last_rejected.quote: he at the same time indicates
last_rejected.why: ὁμοῦ means 'together with' other things, not 'at the same time' as a temporal adverb.
last_rejected.ruling: ὁμοῦ can function adverbially as ‘at the same time’; translation captures the sense.

last_rejected.why: εὐθύνει here means 'exposes/convicts', not 'corrects'; and 'their' is wrong antecedent.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐθύνει can mean ‘correct’ or ‘set straight’; using ‘corrects’ is acceptable, ‘their’ is a minor nuance.

last_rejected.why: κόσμῳ is dative of reference ('in the world'), not 'upon the world'.
last_rejected.ruling: κόσμῳ is dative of reference; ‘come upon the world’ is a reasonable rendering.
